paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: the God who walks among His people cares about every corner of their life. Moses moves from who may enter the assembly, to the army camp, to money, to vows, to a neighbor's field, and it all hangs on one truth. The LORD is near, and the people who belong to Him are to live like it (Deut 23:14). Even the camp's cleanup rules were about that: "Your camp must be holy, lest He see anything unclean among you and turn away from you." Yes, even the digging tool. I once thought holiness was only for church hour, and then Moses brings a shovel.

Look at how that closeness shapes the way people treat each other. Moses says to Israel, "Do not despise an Edomite, for he is your brother," and he tells them to let a runaway slave live "wherever he chooses" and "Do not oppress him" (Deut 23:7, 16). Interest was not to be charged to a brother, so the LORD could bless everything their hands touched (Deut 23:19-20). A neighbor's vineyard and grainfield got the same care: eat your fill, but don't haul it off (Deut 23:24-25). Holy living shows up in how you treat the people right next to you.

Then there's the mouth. Moses says, "Be careful to follow through on what comes from your lips, because you have freely vowed to the LORD your God with your own mouth" (Deut 23:23). Nobody forced the vow, so the words are yours to keep. So here's what I want you to carry, baker: God is near, His people are kind, and your word counts. Think before you promise, and when you do promise, show up. And Moses isn't done preaching yet, so stay with me.
